x: The team finished fourth, Chris Steer was fourth individual and 'old man' Jackie Brown convincingly won the Vet's prize. John Walker provided vocal accompaniment.

John Walker, inspite of a recent spell of "special coaching and altitude training" by brother Charlie in the Isle of Wight, found Charlie Smart just too good for him again, as did Glimpy Jones---rumours that Glimpy travelled down overnight and went round the course in the morning have not yet been proved!.

He will, of course, still be pleased to see anyone who cares to call but rumour has it that he is hoping to build up enough speed training during the coming months to be able to escape quickly out of the backdoor when John Walker appears to deliver one of his famous three hour lectures on his recent training and races!
So much so that he spent a great deal of time collecting together all the information he could find, with a view to writing the book that John Walker would like to see.

Front Cover: Following a remarkable season including winning the AAA's 1500m title, second in the Commonwealth 1500m and new club mile record John Gladwin beat a class field including John Walker, Jack Buckner, Tim Hutchins and Dave Moorcroft to win the London Mile in record time.

There were also some former stars who were beginning to fade including those great sprinters Pietro Mennea and Allan Wells (third and fourth in the 200m), and John Walker (NZ) and Mike Boit (Kenya) - ninth and twelth in the 1500m.
